ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ (١)).
The apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا» is (عَلِمَتْ).

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ (٦) الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ (٧)).
(مَا غَرَّكَ) is an interrogative and nothing else; had it been an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), He would have said «مَا أَغَرَّكَ».
(عَدَلَكَ) with doubling (عَدَّلَكَ) means: He made your form upright; and without doubling (عَدَلَكَ) it has this same meaning. It may also mean: He turned you away from a disliked form.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا شَاءَ): «مَا» may be redundant (zāʾida), or conditional; on both views the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «صُورَةٍ», and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «رَكَّبَكَ عَلَيْهَا» (He assembled you in it).
(فِي) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رَكَّبَكَ». It is also said that the clause has no position, because «فِي» is attached to one of the two verbs, so the whole is a single statement; the interrogative was merely placed before what it properly belongs to.

ukberi-tibyan:10-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ (١٠) كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ (١١) يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ (١٢)).
(كِرَامًا) is a naʿt (adjective), and likewise «يَعْلَمُونَ»; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they write knowing.

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ (١٤) يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ (١٥)).
The words of the Exalted (يَصْلَوْنَهَا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the khabar (predicate), or a naʿt (adjective) of «جَحِيمٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ (١٩)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ): it is read in the nominative, i.e. «هُوَ يَوْمُ» (it is a day); and in the accusative on the implied form «أَعْنِي يَوْمَ…» (I mean the day…). It is also said that the implied form is «يُجَازَوْنَ يَوْمَ» (they will be recompensed on the day), indicated by the mention of «الدِّين» (the Judgement). It is also said that it properly should be nominative,
but it was given a fatḥa according to the rule of the adverb (ẓarf), as in the words of the Exalted (وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذَلِكَ). According to the Kufans it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. And Allah knows best.
